sentenceSets.sentence: The two factions agreed to parley before any formal positions had been committed to print.

answerChoices.reasoning: Negotiation means trading terms back and forth, but the sentence places this meeting before either side has set down a position, so there is nothing yet on the table to trade.
Arbitration requires an outside party empowered to decide between the two sides, and the sentence shows the factions themselves agreeing to meet.
A mediator stands apart from the dispute, whereas the subject of the verb here is the two disputing factions, who cannot stand between themselves.
Bargaining presumes each side has something to concede and a stated demand, which the clause about nothing being committed to print rules out.
Convening is what a single body does when it calls itself into session, while the sentence describes two separate factions agreeing to come together.
Reconciliation is an outcome, and the sentence records only that the two sides agreed to sit down, with nothing settled.
Litigation runs through a court and requires filed claims, which is precisely the sort of formal commitment the sentence says has not yet happened.
Capitulation is one side giving way, but both factions are named as equal parties to the agreement.
Breaking up the factions would leave no one to arrive at positions, formal or otherwise.
Renunciation requires something already declared to give up, and the sentence says nothing has been put in writing yet.
Gloating presupposes a victory, while the sentence describes a stage at which neither side has even stated its terms.

sentenceSets.sentence: Under a white flag the besieged garrison sent a young officer out through the gate to parley with the enemy commander.

answerChoices.reasoning: Haggling is bickering over a price, which has no place in a scene of a garrison under siege sending an officer through its own gate.
Surrender would mean handing over the garrison, but only one officer goes out, and the white flag signals a request to talk rather than a transfer of the position.
A petition is a one-way appeal submitted to an authority over you, while the officer is sent to speak face to face with the opposing side's commander.
To remonstrate is to protest a wrong, and nothing suggests the garrison has a grievance to press; it is a besieged force seeking contact with the enemy.
Fraternizing is informal mixing with the other side, which does not fit an officer dispatched formally under a flag of truce.
Conspiracy is secret, yet the white flag and the open passage through the gate make this the most visible act possible.
A skirmish is fighting, which the white flag exists specifically to suspend.
Reconnoitering is covert observation of enemy positions, but the officer is sent to meet the commander, not to look around unnoticed.
Flight would not be announced with a white flag or aimed at the enemy commander.
A single officer on foot under a truce flag cannot be conducting an artillery attack.
A garrison under siege has nothing to celebrate, and the errand is directed at the opposing commander.

sentenceSets.sentence: The neighbors parleyed across the fence for the better part of an hour about the disputed line of hedges before anyone thought to mention lawyers.

answerChoices.reasoning: A quibble is a petty objection about something trivial, but the subject here is a contested property line serious enough that lawyers come up at the end.
Bickering is snapping back and forth, which does not match an exchange that lasted most of an hour and only afterward turned adversarial.
Wrangling implies the dispute was already hostile throughout, yet the sentence marks the mention of lawyers as the turn, implying the hour before it was not yet a fight.
Commiseration means sharing sorrow over a common misfortune, and these two stand on opposite sides of the hedge line they disagree about.
Gossip is idle talk about absent third parties, while the subject of this hour is the boundary between the speakers' own properties.
Sparring suggests testing blows for practice, but each neighbor has a real stake in where the hedges fall.
Equivocation is deliberate vagueness by one speaker, and the sentence describes an exchange between two people rather than anyone's evasiveness.
Temporizing means stalling to avoid committing, which sits oddly with two neighbors who spend an hour on the substance of the hedge line.
Reminiscence looks back fondly at the past, whereas this conversation concerns a present disagreement headed toward lawyers.
Sleeping is incompatible with an hour of talk about a contested boundary.
Brooding is done silently and alone, but the sentence has two neighbors speaking to each other across a fence.
